name: explainroo (narrated explainer videos and product demos)
what: A script (script.md) and drawn scenes (scenes.js) become a narrated MP4 with word-timed visuals, subtitles, chapters and a cover - local voice (Kokoro), word timing (Whisper), Chrome draws the frames, ffmpeg writes the video. No account, no key.
weights: Kokoro + Whisper base.en, about 400 MB, fetched once into the tool's models folder

init.what: Make a new video project folder (video.json, script.md, scenes.js). Then write script.md (the narration) and scenes.js (the drawings) - read the project's AGENTS.md via the docs action first.

project.what: folder name for the project, inside the job's folder

voice.what: a Kokoro voice (voices action lists them)

docs.what: Print explainroo's guide for coding agents (how to write script.md and scenes.js) - read it before writing them.

voice.what: Make the narration and its word timings from script.md.

check.what: Find layout, timing and pronunciation problems before rendering (fails on an error).

sheet.what: A contact sheet of the whole video (out/sheet.jpg) to look at before rendering.

render.what: Render the video (draft quality first: quality fast).

video.what: the MP4 to write, inside the job's folder

verify.what: Check the rendered video: loudness, black frames, silence, narration clarity (fails on an error).

notes: Needs Node.js 20.11+, ffmpeg and Chrome or Chromium. Leave the image/clip commands alone: they cost money (OpenRouter). AMAL's own pictures go in the project's assets/ folder instead.
verified_from: src/cli.js HELP (init, voice, check, sheet, render --quality --out, verify --file, docs, voices, doctor --fetch) and package.json (bin explainroo, 0.5.0) at 1916129d

name: Open Code Review (Alibaba's AI code reviewer)
what: Reviews a repository's changes (uncommitted work, a commit, or a branch against another) with deterministic git tools plus an agent, and writes line-level findings as JSON. Runs on AMAL's own free models.

review.what: Review a git repository's changes: what is not committed yet (default), one commit, or a branch against a base. Writes the findings as JSON.

repo.what: the git repository (a project folder of this job)

base.what: base branch or commit to compare from, '-' for uncommitted work

head.what: branch or commit to review ('-' with a base = HEAD; a commit alone reviews that commit)

notes: Needs git 2.41+ and Node.js (npm). The reviewer's model is AMAL's driver at {amal_llm} (free models only).
verified_from: README (npm @alibaba-group/open-code-review, ocr review / --from --to / --commit, --format json --output) and the configuration docs' OCR_LLM_URL / OCR_LLM_AUTH_TOKEN

name: Cutroom (narrated shorts: voice, captions, music and the cut)
what: A script and the job's own pictures and clips become a finished short (9:16, 16:9 or 1:1): the voice, word-by-word captions in the platforms' safe zone, a slow camera move on every picture, transitions, music under the voice - each one set by AMAL's settings. Built on MoneyPrinterTurbo (MIT): its voice (edge-tts), captions (faster-whisper) and render.
weights: faster-whisper is fetched by the tool when subtitles use it

short.what: Cut a short video from a script and the pictures and clips in a folder of this job, in their order; the MP4 lands in the job's folder.

media.what: folder of this job with the pictures and clips to use (AMAL's renders)

script.what: the narration word for word, or '-' to have it written

options.what: how it looks and sounds, as JSON: captions, caption_style (Word pop / Word by word / Sentence), caption_place (Lower third / Bottom / Middle / Top), caption_size, caption_color, caption_outline, caption_box, font (Bold / Clean / Display / Script), voice_speed, voice_volume, music, music_volume, music_file, motion (Slow zoom / Still), transition (Cut / Fade / Slide / Zoom / Mixed), cut_seconds, fit (Fill / Fit), language - see the runner

notes: The online stock footage providers need keys of their own; the default here is local footage from the job, so nothing is paid. edge-tts needs the internet.
verified_from: cli.py (--video-subject, --video-script, --video-source local, --video-materials, --video-aspect, --voice-name, --task-id; prints {task_id, result{videos}}) and config.example.toml (llm_provider, openai_base_url, openai_api_key, openai_model_name) at c2353548

name: MarkovJunior (procedural levels, dungeons and voxel buildings)
what: Probabilistic rewrite rules grow mazes, dungeons, caves, cities, islands and voxel buildings - 159 ready models (DungeonGrowth, ModernHouse, SeaVilla, CarmaTower, Island...). 2D models give PNG maps, 3D models .vox voxel buildings - level layouts for a game.

generate.what: Grow one model (a name from models/ such as DungeonGrowth, BasicDijkstraDungeon, Cave, ModernHouse, SeaVilla, Apartemazements) into PNG maps or .vox voxel files in a folder of this job.

model.what: the model's name (list action shows them)

notes: Brings Microsoft's .NET SDK itself when the machine has none (their own installer script, into the tool's folder: no administrator rights, nothing changed on the system). .vox opens in MagicaVoxel and imports into Blender and Godot.
verified_from: source/Program.cs (reads models.xml and resources/ from the folder it runs in, writes output/), models.xml attributes (name, size, d, length, width, height, amount, seed), MarkovJunior.csproj (net10.0) at 42aaf24b

name: ArtCraft (intentional crafting engine for images and video)
what: A desktop IDE for directing AI images and video like a film set - stage 3D scenes, pose, frame and paint, then generate - instead of rolling the dice on a prompt. Opened beside AMAL for hands-on art direction.

install.manual: Download the desktop app from the repository's releases (or build it with cargo per its README) and install it; AMAL opens it from the Library's Apps once it is installed. The PC already has an Artcraft folder in the user's home.

notes: A desktop app, not a command line: AMAL's agents open it for the owner; its generations land in his folders and the Library picks them up.
verified_from: repository description and README (Rust desktop app, image and video generation IDE)

name: Career (resume, cover letter, job search, portfolio)
what: A resume kept as JSON Resume data becomes a typeset PDF in one of seven RenderCV themes, with a picture of each page to look at; a cover letter set in the same type; jobs found on LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, Google and ZipRecruiter with JobSpy (title, company, place, pay, the link to apply, the posting); a self-contained portfolio page from the resume and chosen pictures and videos.

resume.what: Typeset a resume (JSON Resume data) as a PDF; a PNG of each page and the RenderCV YAML land beside it.
the resume as JSON Resume data

letter.what: Set a cover letter (Markdown) as a PDF in the resume's type, the resume's name and contact on top.

resume.what: the resume (for the name and contact)

jobs.what: Find job postings: every one found with its title, company, place, pay, link and description, as jobs.json and a table in jobs.md.

terms.what: what to search for: a job title and a skill or two

location.what: a city and state or a country; '-' for anywhere

sites.what: comma-separated: indeed, linkedin, glassdoor, google, zip_recruiter

portfolio.what: A self-contained portfolio web page (index.html and its media folder) from the resume and the pictures and videos in a folder.

media.what: folder of this job with the pictures and videos to show, or '-'
